chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Three [types of people] will not enter Paradise: the blood-shedder, the drinker of wine (alcohol), and the go-between of gossip.

key_terms.السَّافِكُ لِلدْمِ: The blood-shedder; one who kills or sheds blood unjustly
key_terms.مَشَّاءٌ بِنَمِيمَةٍ: The go-between of gossip; one who spreads rumors to cause enmity

ai.seo_question: Who are the three people that will not enter Paradise according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights three distinct sins that serve as a barrier to Paradise: the murderer (*al-safaak lil-dam*), the alcoholic (*sharib al-khamr*), and the gossip-monger (*musha' bi-namima*). This triad emphasizes the destruction of life, the impairment of reason, and the corruption of social bonds, respectively, reflecting the Shia emphasis on both individual piety and communal harmony. The term *namima* specifically refers to carrying tales between people to cause enmity, a grave social sin often linked to the breakdown of trust within the community.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-244 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Abdullah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sin’an, on the authority of some men that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “
The following three groups of people will not enter Paradise: those who shed blood; the alcoholics; and those who go around to gossip.”
